Measure diethyl phenylmalonate at 10/1 and 50 uL, predicted 11.24/22.37 mL. At the same loading, 3726956d81fe3954e5b7 measured 18.43/30.51 at 20/1, whereas 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e unexpectedly measured 5.55/11.63 at 50/1. This interior label tests whether retention rises toward 20/1 before reversing, or whether the 20/1 observation is locally exceptional.

Measure diethyl phenylmalonate at 20/1 and 100 uL, predicted 14.28/27.45 mL. Relative to the 50-uL observation 3726956d81fe3954e5b7, only sample volume changes. Together with the selected 10/1 row, this tests whether the unexpectedly retained 20/1 region persists at another amount and constrains loading sensitivity. A single contrast cannot distinguish a causal loading effect from unrecorded variation.

Measure ortho-methoxyacetophenone at 20/1 and 50 uL, predicted 8.26/26.06 mL. This completes a two-ratio, two-amount comparison with ebdeaba52880c7eade16, c82167c626a1495ef750 and 52b9af4df1f1e7cd4d9b. At 50/1, reducing sample volume from 150 to 50 uL changed onset from 1.01 to 11.65 mL while completion stayed near 23.7. The new label tests whether this endpoint-specific association also occurs at 20/1.

Measure tetralone at 10/1 with the same loading as its 20/1 and 50/1 observations, predicted 8.48/22.45 mL. Rows 1668026caa5d708642cf and 52348febee6695107c49 measured 13.52/30.38 and 22.75/48.88; the latter rejected the acquisition model's predicted flattening. This interior anchor constrains where the solvent response develops after retraining.

Measure the seven-membered fused ketone m179 at 10/1, predicted 5.50/17.67 mL. Its same-loading 5/1 and 20/1 observations ac975c791f030093081f and 8b8becd233748ccae9e3 measured 5.78/14.77 and 6.13/23.54. Paired with selected tetralone at 10/1, this tests whether ring-size transfer preserves their different onset responses instead of imposing tetralone's correction on both.

Measure para-methoxybenzaldehyde at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 30.72/51.68 mL. Its same-loading 10/1 observation 319e89d7000731f64e7f had early onset but late completion, 4.78/36.82. The predicted large onset increase remains untested. This probes endpoint-specific solvent response in a common aromatic aldehyde motif and complements the pending acetoxybenzaldehyde baseline.

Measure para-methylthioacetophenone at 10/1 and 150 uL, predicted 10.84/28.30 mL. Pending 91cd087e44e7a3364533 uses identical loading at 5/1 and predicts 13.49/30.46, so the current model predicts both endpoints decreasing with weaker eluent. This paired response test checks that reversal. Measured sulfur-containing aldehyde f4331eb64b6774466836 and methoxyacetophenone 122fbec0df9ecf1c5d89 provide related, but differently loaded, structural references.

Measure ethyl para-aminobenzoate at 5/1 and 50 uL, predicted 14.64/25.98 mL. Its measured 2/1 row 70593725787c65a74951 gives 10.81/22.83 at 100 uL, while the aminobenzonitriles showed steep growth by 5/1 in ad833f34f6b91872362d and a60552f4d1a5ced4641f. This tests whether the model correctly distinguishes aminoester from aminonitrile response; the amount difference prevents interpreting the comparison as a pure solvent effect.

Measure ethyl meta-aminobenzoate at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 11.63/21.56 mL. The molecule has measured strong-eluent anchors, including 9a9324fbb6b1e17e7743 at 1/1, but lacks a measured weaker-eluent response. Alongside selected para aminoester and observed ortho aminoester 3aed7873d2fd1cf48684, this tests positional transfer. Different sample amounts, loading volumes and loading solvents must remain explicit covariates.

Measure pyridyl ethyl ketone m66 in pure EA at its existing 100-uL loading, predicted 7.31/15.65 mL. Same-loading observations 4659b6752f23c0b85f08 and 49201b5817f204116f7f give 18.98/55.06 at 2/1 and 47.37/119.31 at 5/1. A strong-eluent endpoint distinguishes an overall molecular retention offset from a sharply solvent-dependent response in this severe historical failure region.

Introduce ethyl 2-bromo-2-methylpropanoate at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 9.17/9.32 mL. The almost coincident endpoints and V1 quantile-order inconsistency are model diagnostics, not measured errors. The closest labeled ester family includes methyl 2-bromo-2-methylpropanoate and ethyl 2-bromopropanoate, with 90d8a6d3f4fbe760dd4e and b6685aed98359c179cd7 as measured references. This tests transfer across ester alkyl identity and alpha substitution in the early-eluting region.

Introduce ortho-tolualdehyde at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 8.68/17.91 mL. Meta-tolualdehyde at 50/1 measured 11.59/24.54 in 85956151bfe869ac5ee6, and 2,4-dimethylbenzaldehyde at matched sample volume measured 9.95/27.78 in 8b06ec38a7e5999edfa6. This tests positional and steric transfer across ordinary aromatic aldehydes; the meta reference has different loading conditions.

Measure naphthalen-2-ylmethanol at 1/1 and 50 uL, predicted 16.62/38.42 mL. Its identically loaded 2/1 observation 7c0c324643799c918828 is 12.96/23.61. The model therefore predicts substantially later completion in stronger eluent. This directly tests an unusual response and complements pending 5/1 at 150 uL without duplicating that experiment.

Measure 2-(naphthalen-1-yl)ethanol at 2/1 and 100 uL, predicted 15.64/26.40 mL. Its same-loading 1/1 observation 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8 is 18.27/33.28. Together with the selected naphthylmethanol row, this tests whether the predicted 1/1-to-2/1 reversal is shared by two related aromatic alcohols or is a transferred model artifact.

Measure the ether-containing aryl ketone m106 at 10/1 and 100 uL, predicted 11.41/25.96 mL. Its supplied measured anchor 265b6eb5a10a34c937b1 is pure EA, 5.71/8.96, at identical loading. This tests the combined influence of a remote ether and a trifluoromethyl-substituted aryl ketone beyond a strong-eluent baseline, extending coverage of multifunctional carbonyl response.

Measure 1,3-dibenzoylbenzene at 10/1 with identical loading to its existing curve, predicted 7.32/23.76 mL. Observations 17fd49e7bf1b8c8b08f7, 855456da9ea892f7216b and 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 give 6.03/18.17 at 5/1, 18.76/48.89 at 20/1 and 44.91/98.73 at 50/1. This resolves the predicted delayed rise between 10/1 and 20/1 and helps distinguish separated aromatic carbonyls from the much earlier-eluting beta-diketones.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environment and substitution position determine solvent-response slopes; the steep aminonitrile and pyridyl-ketone responses need not transfer uniformly to aminoesters.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels constrain structure-by-solvent interactions across several nitrogen environments and discourage a common nitrogen retention correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do meta and para aminoesters retain their predicted modest 5/1 response, and does the pyridyl ketone return to early elution in pure EA?

hypotheses.content: Phenylmalonate's measured reversal between 20/1 and 50/1 invalidates a simple monotone extension for this recorded series. Whether it reflects a repeatable local response, amount sensitivity, or isolated experimental variation remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest 37.55-mL completion overestimate shows that transferring a conventional ester response can fail badly. Local labels can constrain the exceptional region without spreading its correction across all esters.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 50-uL 10/1 label connect to the retained 20/1 observation, and does that 20/1 region persist when sample volume doubles?

hypotheses.content: Ortho-methoxyacetophenone has an observed amount association that affects onset far more than completion at 50/1; its persistence at 20/1 is unknown.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An endpoint-specific loading interaction is more consistent with the measured contrast than shifting V1 and V2 together. Replication is absent, so the association should not yet be treated as causal.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 20/1, does reducing sample volume from 150 to 50 uL delay onset while leaving completion comparatively stable?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic carbonyl retention requires topology- and substituent-specific solvent responses, with onset and completion sometimes changing differently. Recent failures do not support a uniform correction for aromatic ketones or aldehydes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Aromatic carbonyls occupy many catalog rows. Matched response anchors and close structural comparisons can improve interpolation across ring sizes, functional-group arrangements, and substitution patterns.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do tetralone and dibenzoylbenzene develop their retention rise, does methoxybenzaldehyde develop late onset at 50/1, and is the predicted methylthioacetophenone reversal real?

hypotheses.content: The model predicts lower retention at 2/1 than at 1/1 for two naphthalene-containing alcohols. This may be a shared recorded response or an incorrectly transferred solvent-ratio pattern.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The measured anchors establish only one side of each comparison. Completing both matched-loading contrasts tests a shared model behavior in hydrogen-bond-donating aromatic compounds without assuming monotonicity is universal.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do both alcohols actually show the predicted 1/1-to-2/1 decrease, or does one or both follow the usual normal-phase trend toward later elution in weaker solvent?

feedback_interpretation: The latest labels sharpened several hypotheses and reduced the value of others. Meta-aminobenzonitrile at 5/1 measured 34.93/86.44, supporting steep solvent sensitivity but a smaller response than the para isomer; para at 1/1 was predicted accurately. I therefore extend nitrogen learning to aminoesters and the strong-eluent pyridyl-ketone baseline. Dibenzylamine at 2/1 measured 8.75/16.75 at 100 uL and 8.83/17.21 at 50 uL in 6defbf00ecb558b77d50 and f6c49d6bc4b677f17278. This weakens any general loading-offset interpretation of its large 5/1 contrast, and I do not spend another label on its low-ratio amount variants. Ortho-methoxyacetophenone's lower-load 50/1 result changed onset by 10.64 mL relative to the higher-load observation but barely changed completion, motivating a matched 20/1 contrast. Phenylmalonate's 5.55/11.63 result at 50/1 rejected the anticipated monotone extension and produced the largest recent supplement error; it now warrants local discrimination rather than a generic ester correction. Tetralone's 22.75/48.88 result rejected predicted flattening, whereas deoxybenzoin, fluoropropiophenone, the hydrophobic benzoate and the lactone interior transferred reasonably well, lowering their immediate follow-up priority. Acetoxybenzaldehyde still showed underestimated completion at 2/1, but its pending 1/1 measurement already supplies the next baseline. Pending-CW outcomes separately exposed underestimation for para-methoxyacetophenone and the multifunctional methacrylate, while salicylaldehyde completion was overestimated. These opposite errors reinforce endpoint- and connectivity-specific learning. All errors discussed are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch complements the pending measurements through a few explicit local experiments and structural transfer tests. Phenylmalonate receives an interior ratio and a fixed-ratio amount contrast because its latest reversal cannot be interpreted from one exceptional label. Ortho-methoxyacetophenone receives the missing corner of a two-ratio, two-amount comparison. Tetralone and its seven-membered analogue test ring-size transfer; dibenzoylbenzene, methoxybenzaldehyde and the remote-ether ketone constrain different carbonyl response curves. Methylthioacetophenone forms a matched-loading solvent comparison with a pending row. The aminoester selections and pyridyl-ketone baseline extend nitrogen learning beyond already measured high-retention examples. Two matched aromatic-alcohol contrasts test a shared predicted reversal, while an unmeasured bromoester and positional aldehyde test transfer in more ordinary retention ranges. I considered the supplied pool's many duplicate tuples and near-identical amount predictions; extra related rows are retained only where they answer a specific response or loading question. The pending arm already covers several early esters, aromatic alcohols and strong-eluent baselines, so these supplements emphasize complementary relationships. Quantile widths and CW distances are diagnostic evidence rather than calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The intended gain is improved V1/V2 structure-condition interpolation and endpoint-specific transfer across the Row-distribution, with unrecorded experimental variation limiting mechanistic attribution.
